title: System Overlay
concept: One order for any hard conversation, designed so it ends with who does what. It comes at three speeds: quick, standard, and for when it’s already a fight.
whenToUse: Quick (about 90 seconds): you can hear the sniping start. Standard: you need to raise something touchy, ask for a change, make a repair or decide something together. Already a fight: it’s started, or it’s the one you keep having, and you can still be kind to each other. If you start going in circles, find the step you skipped and go back to it. A serious hurt needs the slow version, Full Recovery. Quick version: “Restart — same team.” One warm sentence each, name the one problem you’re both stuck in, then either one ask or a Pause + Return.
steps: Warm up — say the warmest true thing you can. Remind each other you’re on the same team. Already a fight? First check you’re both calm; if either of you is flooded, take a Pause + Return.
Make it safe — say out loud that the relationship isn’t at risk tonight.
Say what happened — describe it, then say how it felt and what it meant to you. The one listening hears it in order: how it landed, then what would help, and only then their side.
Ask for one thing — make it specific and doable, with a time to do it by. If it’s a change you’ll want to see, make it a Proof item.
Agree on next steps — decide who does what, by when, and when you’ll check back in.

phrases.text: I love us, and I’m not trying to fight.
When X happened, I felt Y; the impact was Z.
Can we try ___ this week and check in on ___?

working: B opens with something kind, says it isn’t a breakup talk, then: “When you scrolled while I talked, I felt dismissed and shut down.” A hears how it landed before explaining. B makes one ask: ten phone-free minutes at night. They try it for a week and check in on Friday.
notWorking: A opens with “Why didn’t you text about the pickup?” and nothing kind first. A cross-examines, B goes quiet, and by nine they’re both arguing about the tone, not the pickup.
activity: A 12-minute practice run: pick something low-stakes, use all five steps out loud, and take turns keeping each other to the order. Then try the quick version once on a minor gripe.
